inapplicable.backendStatusMissing: This detection run says nothing at all about this backend — we have not measured it, so we are not calling it unsupported either.

hw.title: Your hardware
hw.unifiedMemory: Unified memory (VRAM shared with system RAM)
hw.noGpu: Checked — this machine has no usable GPU
hw.reasonPlatformUnsupported: Not applicable on this platform — this backend exists only on Apple platforms (macOS)
hw.reasonProbeFailed: The probe did not run this round, so **nothing at all was measured** about this backend. This is not "your machine does not support it".
hw.reasonDisabledAfterFailures: Disabled automatically after repeated failures — that is **a guard on our side**, not a conclusion about your hardware. Re-running the self-test lets it try again.
hw.reasonNotInstalled: The backend pack is not installed, so **nothing was measured** about it this round. This is not "your machine does not support it". To install it, see "Acceleration backend packs" below.
hw.reasonNotProbedThisRun: Installed, but this detection run never loaded it — that is **no information, not a fault**. Select it as the active backend, or run the self-test on that pack, to get a real answer.
hw.reasonNoUsableDevices: It loaded, but **not one of the devices it reported is usable** (typically only a software renderer) — it falls back to the CPU.
hw.reasonEnumeratedNone: It loaded, and **enumerated no device at all** — most likely the driver is missing or too old.
hw.avx2Unknown: · AVX2 support could not be determined
hw.gpuNotProbed: Not checked yet — no GPU-capable backend was loaded this run (GPU enumeration is done by the probe that ships with a backend pack)
hw.gpuAdvisorySeen: The system does report an adapter: {{adapters}} — so we can see the card, we just have no backend pack installed that can use it (possible: {{backends}})
hw.gpuProbedUnusable: No usable GPU was enumerated — but the system reports {{adapters}} is present, so the gap is on our side, not "you have no GPU"
hw.gpuVirtualUndetermined: "{{adapter}}" is a display adapter provided by a virtual machine — we cannot tell whether a real GPU sits behind it. Install the {{backends}} backend pack and probe once to find out.

recorder.paraformerTradeoff: Trade-off: no word-level timestamps (captions highlight per sentence, not per word), numbers are spelled out, and English comes out lowercase.
recorder.turboTradeoff: Whisper models give word-level timestamps and handle numerals and proper nouns better, at the cost of being far slower (about 22 minutes for an hour of audio on CPU only).
recorder.wordLevelUnavailable: This engine has no word-level timestamps — captions highlight per sentence

recorder.insecureAlternative: Importing a local media file or a link is unaffected — transcription, summary and mindmap all work.

recorder.overrun: The network could not keep up and some audio frames were dropped (words may be missing). The original recording is unaffected.

wsError.asrWorkerNotImplemented: Browser-based recognition is not available in this version.

proxy.title: Network proxy

modeHint.off: All requests go direct. On mainland-China networks Hugging Face and GitHub are usually unreachable, so model downloads will fail.
modeHint.system: Reads HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY / NO_PROXY from the environment. With none set this behaves exactly like a direct connection, which is why it is the default.
modeHint.manual: Use the addresses below. All three accept credentials embedded in the URL.

proxy.authHint: For authentication, embed it in the URL: http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:7890
proxy.loopbackAlwaysBypassed: Loopback addresses (localhost / 127.x / .local) always bypass the proxy — a locally hosted LLM behind a remote proxy could never work.
proxy.socksFfmpegTitle: With SOCKS, media streaming goes direct
proxy.socksFfmpegDetail: With SOCKS, fetching remote media bypasses the proxy and goes direct (link resolution and downloading are unaffected). To route everything through the proxy, use an HTTP/HTTPS proxy instead.
proxy.unsupported: This daemon does not expose a proxy settings endpoint yet
proxy.unsupportedDetail: You can fill the form in, but saving will fail — it will not pretend to succeed. It will work unchanged once the endpoint ships. Until then, start the daemon with HTTPS_PROXY set.
proxy.verdictProxyDown: The proxy itself is unreachable — check the address, port, and that your client is running.
proxy.verdictAllOk: Proxy works; **all {{n}} target(s) probed this run were reachable**. That covers those targets only, not the download-source table below.
proxy.verdictOkSomeSkipped: Proxy works; **the {{tested}} target(s) we did probe were reachable, and {{skipped}} more were not probed at all** (they matched a noProxy exception and went direct) — untested is not the same as reachable.
proxy.verdictUpstreamBlocked: The proxy works, but some targets were unreachable — the problem is the target or its route, not your proxy.
proxy.verdictUnclassified: At least one probe failed in a way we could not attribute to either side — expand its raw error before ruling either one out.

probeDetail.proxyUnreachableNotSent: could not reach the proxy {{proxyUrl}} — no request was sent to {{target}} at all
probeDetail.proxyRejectedCredentials: the proxy {{proxyUrl}} rejected the credentials (407) — check the username/password; this is not the target's doing
probeDetail.proxyRefusedTunnel: the proxy {{proxyUrl}} answered but refused to open a tunnel to {{target}} (CONNECT was neither 2xx nor 407) — common with corporate proxies that deny by policy; we cannot tell whether the problem is the proxy policy or the target

proxy.sourcesSomeUnreachable: ⚠️ **{{n}} download source(s) are unreachable**: {{list}}. This table and the proxy verdict above **were measured against different targets** — a working proxy does not mean these sources can be downloaded from.
proxy.testUsesSaved: ⚠️ You have unsaved changes. Tests run against the SAVED configuration — save first, or you are reading a stale result.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.probeCaveat: The self-check above asks whether the FEATURE works. The groups below ask whether a COMPONENT is present and loaded. A green light below does not guarantee the feature works.

chunkingReason.noVadModelInstalled: No VAD model installed → chunking falls back to fixed windows
chunkingReason.installedWeightsNotLoadable: whisper.cpp cannot load any of the VAD weights installed here ({{rejected}}) → chunking falls back to fixed windows. Transcription still completes, but sentence boundaries get worse. What you have is most likely the one sherpa-onnx uses; whisper.cpp needs "vad/silero-vad-ggml" — install that from the Models page to get silence-based splitting back.
chunkingReason.runtimeFailure: The VAD step failed to run this time → chunking fell back to fixed windows.

diagnostics.chunkingFixed: VAD unavailable → fixed 30 s windows (transcription still works, sentence boundaries get worse)
diagnostics.chunkingRuntimeFailure: ⚠️ This is not a missing model — the weights are on disk and the VAD step itself failed, so installing the model again will not fix it.
diagnostics.toolchainUnknown: Could not confirm whether the toolchain is complete — this is not "OK", it is "could not check"

selfcheck.title: Feature self-check
selfcheck.unavailableHint: Self-check results did not come back (an older local service does this). The groups below still work, but they only check whether components are present — do not read this blank as "everything is fine".
selfcheck.empty: The self-check returned zero checks. That is itself abnormal; do not read it as "everything is fine".

diagnostics.copyFailed: Copy failed — the browser blocks clipboard access here; select the text below manually

asr.languageInvalid: Invalid language code (expected zh, en, yue, zh-Hans …, or auto). The backend will silently fall back to auto.
asr.autoHint: Auto-detect will not use Paraformer (the backend picks an engine from the language prefix). Choosing Chinese explicitly is faster and more accurate for Chinese audio.

engineUnavailable.modelNotInstalled: no model is installed for it — install one on the Models page to enable it
engineUnavailable.installedButFilesIncomplete: installed ({{ids}}), but the files are incomplete so it cannot load — reinstall it on the Models page
engineUnavailable.overrideDirIncomplete: {{envVar}} points at {{dir}}, and the files this engine needs are not there

uninstall.recordRemovedFilesKept: Uninstalled — the record is gone. But {{n}} file(s) could not be deleted, because the record pointed outside the data folder: {{names}}
uninstall.filesKeptHint: The uninstall went through — no need to press again. Delete those files yourself if you want the space back.
uninstall.recordRemovedFilesFailed: Uninstalled — the record is gone. But {{n}} file(s) could not be deleted and are still on disk: {{names}}
uninstall.filesFailedHint: The uninstall went through — no need to press again. Each file is listed below with where it is and what you can do.

removalFailure.in_use: {{name}} ({{path}}): another program was holding this file open. Close it, or restart once, and try again.
removalFailure.permission_denied: {{name}} ({{path}}): the system did not allow us to delete it. Delete it from an account that has permission. On Windows a file still open in some program reports the same error — close it and try again.
removalFailure.unknown: {{name}} ({{path}}): we could not delete it, and we do not know why. You can delete it yourself at the path above.

secureContext.title: This address is not a secure context — some features are unavailable
secureContext.localhostCaveat: Open http://127.0.0.1:10000 instead (works if you are on the machine running OpenMemo). For remote access, browsers only expose the microphone over https or localhost — this is not browser-specific, switching browsers will not help. Everything else is unaffected.

caps.microphone: **Recording is unavailable** — browsers only expose the microphone in a secure context.
caps.webLocks: Cross-tab leader election is unavailable — each tab opens its own connection.
caps.clipboard: Copy buttons are unavailable — the clipboard API also requires a secure context.
caps.storage: Session storage is blocked — saving still works (the token is kept in memory), but each reload costs one extra handshake.

jobToast.backgroundHint: You can leave this page — it keeps going in the background
jobToast.verifyingHint: Verifying SHA-256. For large models this takes tens of seconds and the bar does not move — that is normal.
jobToast.installingHint: Unpacking and writing to the models folder. This step has no progress scale — please wait.
jobToast.warmingHint: Building the GPU shader cache — happens only once per machine. Takes around 15 seconds and the bar will not move; that is normal.
jobToast.queuedHint: Waiting for a free download lane; it will start automatically.
jobToast.doneModelHint: Ready to use — paste a link on the capture page to transcribe.
jobToast.doneBackendHint: Available now; running jobs keep their current backend.
jobToast.doneRestartHint: Installed, but the local service must restart before it takes effect.
jobToast.blockedHint: Not a failure — it resumes automatically once the condition is met.
jobToast.title: Install and download progress
jobToast.doneNoteHint: The result is in the note — go take a look.
jobToast.failedHint: This task has stopped and will not resume on its own. You can retry it from Tasks; if a reason is shown above, deal with that first.

items.secureContext: {{count}} browser capabilities unavailable at this address (including recording)
items.secureContextHint: Browsers only expose the microphone, clipboard and cross-tab locks over https or localhost. Open http://127.0.0.1 instead (works if you are on the machine running OpenMemo). Switching browsers will not help; everything else is unaffected.
items.multiTab: Cross-tab leader election unavailable; each tab opens its own connection
items.tokenizer: Chinese tokenizer not enabled — Chinese search may be inaccurate
items.vec: Vector search not enabled — semantic search unavailable
items.pipeline: {{count}} component(s) still to install — this is normal on first launch
items.pipelineUnavailable: No downloadable component package for this platform yet ({{count}})

jobBlocked.NO_TRANSCRIPT: This note has no transcript yet. Transcribe it first, then come back and generate the mind map.

jobBlocked.UNKNOWN: The job is on hold, and it did not say what it is waiting for.

components.title: Components & sources
components.intro: Where each component is downloaded from, which version it is pinned to, and whether upstream has a newer one — all of it inspectable.
components.noAutoUpdateDetail: A newer version is only reported here. Whether and when to update is your call — an upstream version bump can change behaviour.
components.updatableTitle: {{n}} component(s) have a newer version upstream
components.sweepNoneDetail: Their upstream state is "unknown", which is not the same as "up to date". Installed components keep working.
components.emptyHint: The component list ships with the app.
components.failedNote: {{n}} component(s) could not reach their upstream this time. **Each card states its own reason and when to retry.** Not knowing does not affect installing or using them.
components.indeterminateNote: {{n}} component(s) returned an upstream version, but it **is not the same numbering scheme as the pinned one, so the two cannot be ordered**. Retrying will not improve it.
components.confirmUpdate:
Replace "{{name}}" (currently {{from}}) with the pinned {{version}}?

· This installs the version pinned in our manifest, not the latest upstream one
· If the download or the verification fails, your current version is left untouched
· ⚠️ Once the update succeeds there is no way back to the old version

Update now?

installedVersion.noVersionRecorded: the install record carries no version number

noUpstream.staticSource: the catalog registers it with upstream.kind = static
noUpstream.notRegistered: components.json registers no upstream for it at all

indeterminate.versionSchemesDiffer: upstream numbers releases in the {{upstreamScheme}} scheme while we pin {{pinnedVersion}}, which is {{pinnedScheme}} — two different schemes cannot be ordered
indeterminate.pinOutsideAllTagFamilies: this repo publishes several tag families at once ({{families}}), and the pinned {{pinnedVersion}} belongs to none of them

failed.rateLimited: upstream is throttling us (HTTP {{status}}); the wait it gave us: {{wait}}
failed.quotaExhausted: the upstream quota is used up{{scope}}; time until it comes back: {{wait}}
failed.quotaExhaustedNoReset: the upstream quota is used up{{scope}}, and upstream did not say when it resets — so clicking again right now will not help; come back later
failed.httpErrorNotQuota: HTTP {{status}}, and this is not a quota problem — {{remaining}} calls were still left at that moment. The repository may have been renamed or made private, or upstream's abuse protection kicked in
failed.httpErrorNoQuotaInfo: HTTP {{status}}, and upstream sent no quota headers at all, so we cannot tell whether this was throttling
failed.timedOut: the request timed out after {{timeoutMs}} ms. We deliberately do not guess why — a timeout is not evidence of any particular cause
failed.noReleaseMatchesTagPattern: no release matches the tag pattern {{tagPattern}}
failed.repoHasNoReleases: this repository has no releases at all
failed.noTagMatchesTagPattern: no tag matches the tag pattern {{tagPattern}}
failed.npmResponseHasNoVersion: the npm registry answered, but its reply had no version field
failed.huggingfaceResponseHasNoSha: HuggingFace answered, but its reply had no sha field
failed.unsupportedUpstreamKind: we do not know how to query an upstream of kind {{upstreamKind}} — this is a catalog configuration problem, not a network one

note.neverChecked: "Not checked" means **we have not asked upstream yet** — it does not mean you are up to date. Press "Check for updates" above to ask.
note.noUpstream: This component **has no upstream release feed we can query** ({{reason}}). **Pressing "Check for updates" will produce nothing for it** — that is not a failure, there is simply no such question to ask.
note.failed: We **asked upstream and got no answer** ({{reason}}) — that is "unknown", not "up to date". The installed version keeps working.
note.indeterminate: Upstream reports **{{upstream}}**, our manifest pins **{{pinned}}**, and the two cannot be ordered ({{reason}}) — we do not know which is newer.

components.bundledNoDownload: Ships with the app; not downloaded separately
components.upstreamNewerMirror: The upstream project {{repo}} has released {{upstream}}; our manifest pins {{pinned}}. **You cannot update from here, because we have not mirrored that version yet** — the binary for this component is not published by upstream (on this platform they ship libraries only, no executables), we build it ourselves and host it at {{binaryRepo}}. **Upstream releasing a new version is not the same as us having mirrored it.**
components.upstreamNewerPinned: Upstream has {{upstream}}; our manifest pins {{pinned}}. **The upstream version cannot be installed from here** — we only install versions whose sha256 we recomputed independently ourselves.
components.upstreamNewerUnknowable: On top of that, **we cannot say which version this machine currently has** ({{reason}}), so this card does not offer to install the pinned version either.
components.pathHint: You can install the newer version onto your system PATH yourself and we will use it directly (restart the app for that to take effect).
components.sha256Local: recomputed independently on this machine after downloading
components.sha256Upstream: digest supplied by upstream; we did not recompute it ourselves
